segments.text: But we're spending a tremendous amount of time and effort on building our military. We largely rebuilt the military during my first term, fortunately. And we're greatly, greatly enhancing—really enhancing it now.

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: We're going to be doing something new: We're bringing back the battleship. And I thought—like, you remember the battleships from—the great Iowa and Alabama and Missouri—those unbelievable scenes that you'd see, "Victory at Sea." You'd see these incredible ships. And I thought they were powerful, but the battleships that we're building are going to be 100 times more powerful than those beautiful works of art.

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: I mean, they were magnificent, all steel. We have the steel now, and we're going to be doing that as an enhancement. But we—our military is very, very strong.

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: You may want to say something about the large fleet of ships that's heading over to the Middle East.

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: Secretary of War Peter B. Hegseth. Well, Mr. President, you had to, like so many other Cabinet members have referenced, rebuild the perception of America. And at the Department of War, that meant reestablishing deterrence.

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: What happened in Afghanistan, what happened in Ukraine—a war that never would have occurred—what happened on October 7 in Israel never would have happened under President Trump.

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: So, as a result, we're having to rebuild how our enemies perceive us. And when President Trump said, "We're not getting a nuclear Iran. You won't have a nuclear bomb," he meant it, and we sent those B–2s halfway around the world, and they never noticed.

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: When he said: "We're not going to tolerate trafficking drugs anymore in our hemisphere. We treat them like the Al Qaida of the western hemisphere," he meant it. And we're executing that.

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: When you said, Mr. President, "We're securing the border," the military was proud to do their part, alongside Homeland Security, to do that.

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: Same thing with—with Iran right now, ensuring that—they have all the options to make a deal. They should not pursue nuclear capabilities, and we will be prepared to deliver whatever this President expects of the War Department, just like we did this month.

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: No other military in the world could have—could have executed the most sophisticated, powerful raid—not just in American history; I would say in world history. What those men did, going downtown, another country, the most secure place in the most secure base, in the middle of the night, without anybody knowing until those simultaneous bombs dropped 3 minutes before the helicopters dropped—no other country could coordinate that. No other President would have been willing to empower those warriors that way to be that effective. And that sends a message to every capital around the world that when President Trump speaks, he means business. And we are reestablishing deterrence at the War Department, Mr. President.

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: Just to finish up on that, the Somalian pirates, over the years, have pirated, stolen many ships. They would get large amounts of money for the ship. You know, you have a billion-dollar ship, and the insurance companies didn't want to fight, because, you know, some of those ships are very flammable. They're carrying millions of barrels of oil. Very flammable, very dangerous situation if they're shot at. So they wouldn't fight.

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: We notified them a number of months ago: Anybody that does that gets the same treatment as a drug dealer sending their drugs in from Venezuela or anybody else. We—as you know, it's 97-percent down by water. So the drugs coming in by sea or by water will—is down 97 percent.

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: Now we're also starting—that was the more difficult route. Now we're starting to do that by land also. It will be—you'll see that happen, as they come in and kill our people with drugs. I think the real number is 300,000 people a year, not 100. But whatever it is, it's a lot of people—hundreds of thousands of people. They're going to get hit.

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: But also, we added to the list the Somalian pirates that go out on a boat—similar-type boat, actually. Not quite as fast, not quite as nice, as you can imagine. But they get the same missile that we give to the people that are bringing drugs. And so far, we haven't seen anybody going out. [Laughter]

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: So the traffic is not being interfered with by people pirating our ships. Not our ships—ships all over the world. I said, "Make it for any country." We're doing the rest of the world a favor. It's a very effective favor.

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: But we see very little pirating nowadays. You used to have ships being taken every single—like two or three a week. These massive ships, they'd be brought in to some place in Somalia, which I don't even know is—is it a country?

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: We have—Ilhan Omar left, and then she gives us lectures on the Constitution of the United States. These people are—what they've done to rip off our country is terrible.

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: But the pirating has essentially stopped. They know that if anybody even makes a move toward a ship, they get the ultimate treatment. They will go to wherever they want to go, but it's probably not going to be to Heaven. I can't imagine. But they get—[laughter]—they get hit very hard, just like a drug dealer—dealer. Just like the boats, the ships that are coming in.

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: Every boat that comes in with drugs on it that we take out, we just saved 25,000 American lives. Each boat is the equivalent of saving 25,000 American—mostly American—but American lives.

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: So I just wanted to let you know that. And Pete's been totally authorized to do that, and they know it's going to happen. And it seems that all of that brisk business that they had has been stopped in its—right in its foot.

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: So I just want to thank everybody for being here. My Cabinet has been amazing. I like this much better than going around for 3 hours. [Laughter]

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: We'll pick on other ones. Pam, you're doing great. We're all doing great. J.D., if you'd like to say something, you can. [Laughter] Would you like to really quickly? He is, after all, the vice president of the United States.

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: Vice President Vance. It's okay, sir. I'm here for the free coffee. [Laughter]

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: I'd just say, it's an honor to serve with this group, and we're doing a lot of good for the American people. I'm very proud of it.

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: Yes. We're very proud of the country. We're very proud of you.

segments.speaker: THE PRESIDENT
segments.text: Thank you very much, everybody. Thank you. Thank you very much. Thank you.
